title: What Is the Better Business Bureau? How the BBB Works
summary: Learn what the Better Business Bureau does, how BBB ratings work, and what accreditation costs to decide whether it’s right for your small business.
body_markdown:
The Better Business Bureau was formed in the early 20th century, branding itself as an organization that exposes scams, frauds, and bad advertising practices. For small business owners, receiving a good rating from the Better Business Bureau can contribute to consumer trust.


While BBB reviews aren’t used as widely as some[other review platforms](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/#google-is-losing-traction-but-ai-and-video-reviews-are-picking-up-speed%C2%A0) , the overall value of customer reviews continues to rise. In 2026,[41% of consumers](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/#in-5-consumers-read-reviews-every-time-they-look-for-a-business) claimed they “always” read reviews before making purchases. The same survey recorded that nearly all consumers—97% of those surveyed—used reviews for local businesses.


Here’s what the BBB does, the organization’s history, and how BBB business accreditation works.


## What is the Better Business Bureau?


The Better Business Bureau (BBB) is a century-old private, nonprofit organization known for providing business reviews and mediating[customer complaints](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-feedback-tools) . The BBB operates as a network of independent regional bureaus throughout the US and Canada, each with its own standards and membership fees.


The BBB seeks to promote trust between consumers and businesses. It maintains an online database of business profiles across the US and Canada, cataloging information like contact information, years in operation, customer reviews, BBB ratings, and business descriptions.


Today’s BBB functions a lot like Yelp or Google Reviews. Customers leave reviews and complaints, and the BBB assesses whether the business has addressed the complaints. The BBB helps mediate business-customer disputes through formal mediation or arbitration when appropriate, and it assigns business ratings from A+ to F, based on complaint history, time in business, transparency, and adherence to BBB standards.


Unlike other review websites, the BBB’s ratings are based on its own[set of standards](https://www.bbb.org/about/overview-of-ratings) , including whether businesses resolve customer complaints and adhere to the BBB’s[advertising standards](https://www.bbb.org/code-of-advertising) . It also warns consumers and businesses about scams and fraud detected by the organization.


Businesses with ratings of B or higher can also pay to become a BBB-accredited business, which lets them flesh out their online profile and display the BBB Accredited Business Seal on their website.


### History of the Better Business Bureau


The BBB’s historical role was far broader than reviews. Formed in 1912, the BBB was a major part of the[Truth-in-Advertising Movement](https://brandingstrategyinsider.com/2008/04/the-truth-in-ad/) , which worked to curb the rise of deceptive advertising. For decades, the BBB was the face of the business-led effort to investigate fraudulent business practices and outlined advertising standards that often guided federal laws. While the BBB is sometimes mistaken for a government agency, the organization is business-led and has never had any official legal or governing authority.


The BBB has significantly scaled back its regulatory advocacy since the 1980s, and now relies heavily on its business database and rating system, where fees and sponsorships collected from businesses bring in the majority of its revenue.


## How the BBB rating system works


The BBB of today is known for its rating system, launched in 2009.[According to the BBB](https://www.bbb.org/about/overview-of-ratings) , ratings are given from A+ to F based on[16 criteria](https://web.archive.org/web/20110729091548/http://www.bbb.org/business-reviews/ratings/) , including:


- Complaint history with the BBB
- Time in business
- Transparency of business practices
- Past violations of laws or licensing regulations
- Past advertising issues


A good BBB rating requires that a business directly engage with the BBB website and resolve customer complaints regularly. It also requires that a business “[honor commitments to the BBB](https://www.bbb.org/about/overview-of-ratings) ,” including abiding by mediation settlements or arbitration awards determined by the BBB. Unresolved complaints can significantly impact a business’s BBB rating, and businesses can lose accreditation if they receive a grade of B- or lower.

## What is BBB accreditation?


BBB accreditation is a designation issued to companies that meet the BBB’s advertising standards, respond promptly to consumer complaints, pay an annual fee, and maintain a BBB rating of B or higher. A business becomes eligible for accreditation after it’s been in operation for at least six months.


The BBB also requires that businesses adhere to its long-standing[advertising standards](https://www.bbb.org/code-of-advertising/) , judged entirely by the BBB. These include ensuring advertising is truthful, disclosing all prices and discounts accurately, and making sure price comparisons and special claims are transparent and accurate.


Businesses that meet all these criteria receive several benefits:


-


A detailed profile page in the BBB database


-


Permission to display the[BBB Accredited Business Seal](https://www.bbb.org/content/dam/0825-austin/bbb-seals/BBB_AccreditedBusiness_Seals.pdf) on their business websites


-


Access to free mediation and arbitration services through the BBB’s dispute resolution system


For many small businesses, however, BBB accreditation is a significant expense. Each BBB regional affiliate has its own fee structure, but annual accreditation fees are usually between $500 and $1,500 for small businesses. Larger organizations may have to pay thousands of dollars more per year, with fee amounts based on the business’s size and the regional BBB’s pricing policies.


Businesses do not need to be accredited to be included in the BBB directory, and the BBB regularly uses other search methods and databases to add non-accredited businesses (again, only requiring that businesses have been in operation for six months or more). Non-accredited businesses can also respond to customer complaints on a voluntary basis; however, they don’t get access to the BBB’s formal mediation and arbitration tools.


## Better Business Bureau FAQ


### What does the Better Business Bureau actually do?


The Better Business Bureau is a business-led nonprofit organization that provides reviews of businesses using an A+ to F rating system, and mediates customer complaints. The BBB also provides scam alerts for businesses deemed to be fraudulent, and flags advertising practices that violate the BBB’s advertising standards.


### Does the BBB have any power?


The BBB has never had any official legal or governing power. However, historically, it’s played a large role in shaping advertising standards with the goal of advancing marketplace trust. Today, the BBB doesn’t play any major regulatory role, and relies on its reputation and rating system to influence business practices.


### Does the BBB charge a fee?


The BBB charges fees for becoming an accredited business. Small businesses generally have to pay between $500 and $1,500, with larger businesses charged more based on factors like the number of employees, number of locations, and annual revenue. However, you don’t have to be accredited by the BBB to be listed in its database or respond to customer complaints. BBB-accredited businesses are able to include more information about their business in the BBB database, and may include the BBB Accredited Business Seal on their website.


### What happens if a business ignores a BBB complaint?


The BBB rating system heavily factors whether a business responds to each complaint in a timely manner. To maintain a good BBB rating, make sure complaints are addressed and the complaint is considered resolved by the BBB.
